subject: Numeracy
title: Big, bigger, biggest
objectives: Children will compare two objects by size.
Children will order three objects from small to big.
content: Big and small, bigger and smaller, and ordering three things by size.
teachingActivities: Always compare two objects side by side; use the words bigger and smaller; introduce the -est words with three objects; use everyday objects such as cups, balls, stones and children’s shoes; keep a fair comparison (same starting line).
learnerActivities: Compare two objects by size and order three objects from small to big.
assessment: Observe whether each child compares two objects by size and orders three objects.
expectedOutcomes: Says which of two is bigger.
Orders three objects by size with support.
crossCurricular: Creative Development: drawing big and small

lessons.title: Big and small
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will say big and small for different objects.
successCriteria: Finds a big and a small thing
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort by colour and size and find pairs.
resources: A big and a small ball
A big and a small cup
Pictures of a big and a small animal
lessons.starter: Hold up a big and a small ball and say "This is big. This is small."
teacherActivities: Show pairs of objects and say big or small.
Ask "Which is big?" for each pair.
Let children find a big and a small thing in the room.
Make big and small shapes with arms and bodies.
learnerActivities: Children point to the big one.
Children stretch big and curl small.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show pairs of objects and say big or small. Children: Children repeat the words.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Which is big?" for each pair. Children: Children point to the big one.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children find a big and a small thing in the room. Children: Child finds objects.
Step 4. Teacher: Make big and small shapes with arms and bodies. Children: Children stretch big and curl small.

practical.title: Big and small hunt
practical.safety: Keep the walk slow and supervised. Do not let children lift heavy objects.

differentiation.support: Offer two very different sizes first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find something bigger than their hand.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is the elephant big or small?
Is the ant big or small?

lessons.conclusion: Make a big shape and a small shape and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about big and small things you see.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say big and small for different objects" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Bigger and smaller
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will compare two objects and say which is bigger or smaller.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort by colour and size and find pairs.
resources: Pairs of similar objects in different sizes
lessons.starter: Put two stones side by side and say "This one is bigger than that one."
teacherActivities: Show how to put two objects side by side to compare.
Ask "Which is bigger?" for different pairs.
Let children compare their own shoes.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to put two objects side by side to compare. Children: Children watch and say bigger.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Which is bigger?" for different pairs. Children: Child points and says bigger.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Which is smaller?" Children: Child points and says smaller.
Step 4. Teacher: Let children compare their own shoes. Children: Child compares two shoes.

practical.title: Compare two
practical.safety: Use clean objects with no sharp edges and wash hands after. Keep shoes tidy.

differentiation.support: Compare objects that are very different in size.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find something bigger than a stone.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the objects away and say bigger and smaller.
lessons.homeConnection: Compare two fruits at home and say which is bigger.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "compare two objects and say which is bigger or smaller" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Biggest and smallest
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will order three objects from smallest to biggest.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort by colour and size and find pairs.
lessons.starter: Show three bears and say "Baby Bear, Mummy Bear, Daddy Bear. Which is the biggest?"
teacherActivities: Put three cups in a row from smallest to biggest.
Mix them up and ask a child to order them.
Ask "Which is smallest? Which is biggest?"
Let each child order a set of three.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put three cups in a row from smallest to biggest. Children: Children watch and say biggest.
Step 2. Teacher: Mix them up and ask a child to order them. Children: Child orders the cups.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Which is smallest? Which is biggest?" Children: Child points to each.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child order a set of three. Children: Child orders objects.

practical.title: Order three
practical.safety: Use unbreakable cups and supervise closely. Keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Order two objects first and then add a third.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to order five objects.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the sets away and say biggest and smallest.
lessons.homeConnection: Order three spoons or cups from smallest to biggest.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "order three objects from smallest to biggest" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Three bears
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will use size words to retell part of the story of the three bears.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort by colour and size and find pairs.
resources: Three bowls, chairs and beds in three sizes
lessons.starter: Say "Today we meet three bears: Daddy Bear, Mummy Bear and Baby Bear."
teacherActivities: Tell the story slowly with the three sizes of bowls.
Ask "Which bowl is for Daddy Bear?"
Match chairs and beds to each bear.
learnerActivities: Child points to the biggest bowl.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Tell the story slowly with the three sizes of bowls. Children: Children listen and point.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Which bowl is for Daddy Bear?" Children: Child points to the biggest bowl.
Step 3. Teacher: Match chairs and beds to each bear. Children: Child matches objects to bears.
Step 4. Teacher: Retell the story together. Children: Children retell with objects.

practical.title: The three bears
practical.safety: Use unbreakable bowls and keep the play gentle. Supervise sharing.

differentiation.support: Match two bowls to two bears first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to add more things in three sizes.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Which bowl is for Baby Bear?

lessons.conclusion: Put the bears away and say good night.
lessons.homeConnection: Tell the story of the three bears at bedtime.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use size words to retell part of the story of the three bears" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 7 size check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child compares and orders by size.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort by colour and size and find pairs.
lessons.starter: Sing the big and small song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: compare, order and three bears.
At each station ask "Which is bigger?" and watch.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: compare, order and three bears. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Which is bigger?" and watch. Children: Child answers with a word.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Size stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and use unbreakable objects. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and compare two objects only.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to order five objects.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says big and small; says bigger and smaller; orders three objects; uses biggest and smallest.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 7
Compares and orders by size with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child compares and orders by size" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
